topic: Guardrail hard block vs message substitution
question_text: When a Bedrock Guardrail intervenes, the API response can show either stop_reason: guardrail_intervened (HTTP 200) or stop_reason: end_turn (HTTP 200) with a replacement message. What is the difference between these two intervention modes?

options.text: guardrail_intervened is a hard block (generation stopped, guardrailAction in body); end_turn with a substituted message looks like a normal response to the client
guardrail_intervened means the response was allowed with a warning
Both are identical — Guardrails always use guardrail_intervened
guardrail_intervened triggers an automatic retry with a different model

explanation: A hard block sets stop_reason to guardrail_intervened and includes amazon-bedrock-guardrailAction in the response body — the client knows intervention occurred. Message substitution returns HTTP 200 with stop_reason: end_turn and a replacement message that is indistinguishable from a normal model response. Guardrails do not retry with another model or return responses with 'warnings'.
